propositions: Empty file_impact is overloaded: it cannot distinguish between undeclared (author forgot) and explicitly none (genuinely no file changes), causing conservative whole-HEAD fallback and container poisoning for both cases.
A single non-closed child with empty file_impact collapses its container's drift scope to empty via poison rule, invalidating the whole container even when siblings have precise path declarations.
The current two-state file_impact model causes P9 lint to nag leaf tickets that truthfully touch no files, generating false advisory findings.
Introducing explicit tri-state file_impact_scope (undeclared, paths, none) with required no_file_impact_reason allows distinguishing genuine no-file-impact claims from silent omissions.
An explicitly declared no-file-impact attestation must remain valid across unrelated commits, while undeclared attestations must still invalidate on any commit.
Container roll-up logic must treat declared-none children as neutral (non-poisoning), permitting accurate inherited drift scope from path-declaring siblings.
